adjudication_notes: Author reply and PEP 661 pickling semantics show that sentinels require matching module/name definitions for pickle round-tripping regardless of identifier naming. Generating arbitrary sentinels was intentional; not an objective code defect.
human_comment: I think this has to be a valid identifier?  That's at least strongly expected, and required for pickle support.  Fortunately `st.text().filter(str.isidentifier)` has an efficient implementation 😁

thread_replies.human_comment:
Hmm, the detail here being the expectation that the variable name assigned to the sentinel is equal to the string passed to the sentinel. This is not a requirement, but it is implied that type hints (and, as you say, pickling) only work if these names match:

> Sentinels are conventionally assigned to a variable with a matching name. Sentinels defined in this way can be used in [type hints](https://docs.python.org/3.15/glossary.html#term-type-hint):

However I doubt our sentinel objects will be picklable (or usable in type hints) regardless of if we enforce no-identifier names, since we're creating them in our own module without an associated variable name; from https://peps.python.org/pep-0661/

> When sentinel() creates a sentinel, it records the calling module as the sentinel’s __module__ attribute. Pickling records the sentinel by module and name. Unpickling then imports the module and retrieves the sentinel by name, so the following round trip preserves identity:

given this I'd weakly prefer to keep generating all sentinel objects here. if someone is asking for arbitrary sentinel objects I think we are already breaking the expectation that they work like "standard" sentinel objects.

maybe we could do something like exec'ing in a temporary module with the correct variable association?
